title: KiteWave Integrators — Hybrid Route Partner Framing
summary: Introductory partner discovery to scope a hybrid GPU onramp integration. Discussed KiteWave's channel/reseller model, routing requirements for Redwood (latency vs cost), VPC/private deployment needs, audit/KMS concerns, and a PF pilot (sandbox + benchmarks). Agreed to exchange spec doc, security pack, and schedule a short perf-run next week.

KiteWave: share topology diagram and expected QPS by tenant (Priya) — due 2026-02-09
Schedule 1-hour perf run for week of 2026-02-09 (Marta/Evan)
action_items: Jordan: upload partner spec + security slide deck to shared drive and email link (due 2026-02-06)
Priya: provide topology diagram and list of top 3 anchor customers for pilot (due 2026-02-09)

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-04
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Marta (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions), Evan (KiteWave Partnerships), Priya (KiteWave Solutions), Samir (KiteWave CTO), Lena (KiteWave Security)
-- auto sections sometimes omitted --
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey, thanks everyone for joining, um, appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Evan Torres: Hey Jordan, Evan here. Priya's on. Samir will be in and out. Lena's on the sec side.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi all.
[00:14] Marta Liu: Marta from Redwood, hi.
[00:16] Diego Ramos: Diego, solutions.
[00:18] Samir Mehta: Samir -- sorry, in another meeting, will pop in around 16:20.
[00:22] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: partner fit/go-to-market, technical fit for hybrid onramp (routing, VPC, private control plane), pilot scope and security/compliance callouts. Sound ok?
[00:32] Evan: Sounds good. For context, KiteWave is a systems integrator/reseller focused on telco and edge SaaS customers, we white-label partner infra and want an onramp that respects our channel billing and routing.
[00:44] Jordan: Perfect. Could you share a bit about expected traffic shapes? QPS, burstiness, multi-tenant separation?
[00:51] Priya: Sure — rough numbers: anchor customers range 50–300 qps peak, but most tenants are bursty, median like 5–10 qps. We expect spiky behavior around events. Latency SLOs vary by customer; telecom ones want sub-200ms for short prompts, others are fine up to 800ms.
[01:12] Marta: Ok that's helpful — Redwood's hybrid routing can route by latency or cost tier. We typically recommend routing latency-sensitive tenants to dedicated pools and longer-tail to cost-optimized quantized variants. Quick caveat: quantized models may degrade quality slightly on longer sequences.
[01:30] Priya: When you say quantized variants, are you talking fp16->int8 on the GPU? We're concerned about hallucination risk.
[01:36] Marta: Yeah, parity depends on workload. For short prompt classification, int8 is usually fine. For long context generative tasks we recommend higher precision or Redwood Dedicated. We'll share model/quant profiles.
[01:50] Evan: From a partner billing perspective we need to meter per-tenant and map to KiteWave's billing system. Does Redwood expose per-token and per-route metrics?
[01:58] Diego: Yes — token-level breakdowns, per-route latencies, and we can emit logs to your SIEM or push usage into your billing pipeline. We can also integrate with third-party metering if needed.
[02:10] Lena: Security first — do you support VPC peering or private control plane? We have customers with strict data residency and no internet egress.
[02:18] Marta: We have Redwood Private for VPC deployments and a private control plane option. For partners, a hybrid approach is common: control plane in our region, data plane in your VPC or on-prem. There was some chatter — um — about KMS integrations. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys.
[02:36] Lena: Good. Audit logs and cert rotation?
[02:39] Diego: We can forward audit logs to your lake, and rotation is supported via KMS/HSM integration. We'll send the security pack.
[02:45] Priya: On routing — how do you handle model fallbacks when dedicated capacity is exhausted? We need deterministic behavior for SLAs.
[02:54] Marta: We support policy-based routing: failover to a compatible model variant, or route to a lower-cost queue with circuit-breaker thresholds. For deterministic SLAs, we recommend reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) with burst capacity reserved for partners.
[03:12] Evan: Does that mean we could configure per-tenant policies so our telco customers always hit the dedicated pool?
[03:17] Jordan: Yes, per-tenant routing policies are supported. You can pin model versions per route, set canary rules, and define fallback policies.
[03:25] Priya: About prefix/KV cache — we heavily rely on local KV caches in our edge nodes. Any constraints?
[03:32] Marta: The runtime supports prefix/KV caching and transparent reuse of the KV cache between requests on the same session. For hybrid edge setups we can do local cache + a synchronized cache layer, but the sync frequency affects staleness. Also, note cross-GPU cache transfer can be expensive at scale.
[03:50] Priya: Hmm, can you run a benchmark that demonstrates per-token cost with KV caching on our expected prompt mix?
[03:57] Marta: Absolutely. We'll need your prompts and a sandbox tenant to run against. That was one of the pilot items we mentioned.
[04:04] Samir: (joins) Sorry, afternoon folks. Quick question — what's the ops overhead for us to manage a private data plane? We need to know on-call and patch windows.
[04:12] Diego: For private deployments we provide an ops runbook, automated updates where possible, and you can choose a managed support add-on. On-call still requires customer-side responsibilities for networking and hardware if on-prem.
[04:26] Samir: And SLA?
[04:28] Jordan: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime/latency targets, and for partners we can discuss a shared SLA matrix in the partner contract. We'll propose options in the spec doc.
[04:38] Evan: Competitors asked about third-party routing — do you integrate with AstraCompute?
[04:43] Marta: We don't directly integrate with AstraCompute's control plane but we can interoperate at the model layer and route requests to whatever pool you choose; there may be additional glue around auth.
[04:52] Lena: On compliance, our telco clients require SOC2 and ISO alignment. Do you have certs and can you provide SOC2 Type II and pen test reports?
[04:59] Diego: Yes, SOC2 Type II is available. We'll share redacted pen-test and our compliance summary.
[05:07] Priya: For pilot success criteria — suggestion: 1) latency <250ms p95 for telco route, 2) end-to-end cost per 1k tokens reduction target vs current provider, 3) zero data exfiltrate incidents in test window. Thoughts?
[05:22] Jordan: Agree, and add stability: 99.9% successful request rate during test. We'll help define the synthetic prompt set.
[05:30] Evan: Timeline? We're hoping to kick pilot in 2–3 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:34] Marta: Yes if we get the topology and sample prompts this week. We'll spin up a sandbox tenant and run three perf passes.
[05:42] Priya: Another technical note: some customers need regional model variants for data residency — can you host model weights in our EU region?
[05:50] Marta: Regional hosting is supported in Redwood Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we have regionally available pools but for strict residency we'd recommend a private data plane in your EU VPC.
[06:02] Samir: Regarding model updates and rollout — we need rollbacks to be fast if quality regresses. How do you handle canary and rollbacks?
[06:10] Diego: We have rollouts with canary percentages, automatic rollback on quality/regression if evals fail, and trace hooks for debugging. We can tie evaluations to your prompt sets.
[06:22] Priya: Good. One friction: mapping our billing to per-tenant metering — we'd like a webhook to push usage events into our billing system, not S3 pulls. Supported?
[06:30] Jordan: Yes, we can emit webhooks and have a streaming usage feed; Diego will follow up with the API spec.
[06:36] Evan: Any red flags from a partner enablement perspective? Training materials, SDKs?
[06:42] Diego: We have SDKs (Python/Node/Go), partner onboarding docs, and a partner portal with playbooks. We'll share playbook access in the next deck.
[06:52] Lena: Quick sec — encryption at rest and in transit? TLS + CMEK?
[06:56] Marta: TLS everywhere, and CMEK via customer-managed KMS. We'll include details in the security pack.
[07:03] Jordan: Ok, let's capture concrete next steps — we'll populate the action items in the follow-up. Also sharing the partner integration spec and latency baseline sheet.
[07:12] Priya: For the perf run, can we also test a quantized 4-bit path? We have lower-cost customers that'd accept slight quality tradeoff.
[07:20] Marta: Yes, we can include a 4-bit/8-bit quantized variant in the comparison. We'll note quality metrics and token cost differential.
[07:28] Evan: For contract mechanics: reseller margin and mapping of committed capacity — will this be in the partner MSA?
[07:34] Jordan: Correct — partner MSA will include reserved capacity terms, revenue share, and support levels. We'll loop legal when it gets formal.
[07:40] Samir: Ops question again: how invasive is the on-prem agent? Our hardware team wants to know if kernel modules or special drivers are required.
[07:48] Diego: For on-prem we ship a containerized runtime and a small agent; GPU drivers still need vendor-supported NVIDIA/AMD drivers and common GPU runtimes. No kernel modules beyond standard drivers.
[07:58] Priya: Any known limitations around multi-tenant tenancy isolation on shared pools?
[08:04] Marta: Isolation is via namespace + runtime policies; for strict isolation we recommend dedicated pools per tenant. Shared pools have strong tenancy boundaries but not hardware-isolation.
[08:15] Evan: Ok great. Anything else we missed?
[08:18] Lena: One more: can you provide a sample SOC2 attestation redacted and details on retention policy for logs?
[08:25] Diego: Yes — retention configurable; we'll include defaults and partner options in the pack.
[08:30] Jordan: Cool. Recap of next steps: we (Redwood) send partner spec, security pack, and baseline sheet by Friday (Jordan). KiteWave shares topology + customer list (Priya). Schedule perf run next week (Marta/Evan). Follow-up meeting after perf run to go over results and commercial terms.
[08:50] Evan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:54] Samir: Thanks, bye.
[08:56] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links. (end)
